text:
matt: Heads up — after the continuous-batching tweak rolled at 07:12, p50 on the small-req route jumped ~30ms and overall throughput down ~8%. Lots of 1-token microbatches in the metrics. Anyone digging?

claire: On it. Pulled traces for the last 30m. The bulk of the extra time is in kernel selection / routing — kernel_switch latency spiked. Seems tiny batches are hitting the slower fallback kernel frequently.

anuj: I grabbed a flameprof of the worker at 07:18. Hot slices:
```
kernel_select: 42.1%
enqueue_wait: 12.3%
batch_merge: 8.7%
kv_lookup: 21.6%
other: 15.3%
```
Noting kv_lookup is non-trivial here too.

matt: That matches the dashboards — kernel_select shows a sharp bump at the same time as the rollout. Any config changes to token_budget or queue policy in the deploy?

henry: We changed token_budget_target downwards in the heuristic to favor latency for small sequences (target -> 4 tokens), which intentionally reduces wait time. But that increases microbatch frequency. Also kernel routing currently prefers quantized kernels only for batch_size >= 4; below that we route to a slower unquantized path.

claire: Config excerpt from the rollout: 
```json
{"continuous_batching": {"token_budget_target": 4, "queue_policy": "prefer-latency", "min_batch_for_fast_kernel": 4}}
```

perf-bot: alert: continuous-batcher.p50 > threshold (small-req) triggered 07:15. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/continuous-batcher-latency

matt: I ran a quick aggregation on microbatch sizes between 07:00-08:00: 
```
size,count
1,  4312
2,  2890
3,  1201
4+, 1023
```
Before rollout same window had size=1 ~900 only. Big delta.

anuj: That explains throughput drop — overhead per-batch dominates at size 1. Also KV cache hit-rate dropped ~2% (same sessions) which suggests more contexts are being split across batches, causing more KV misses and repeated kv lookups.

henry: Two levers: 1) revert prefer-latency flag (raise token_budget_target) to let small requests wait slightly for batch formation; 2) lower the min_batch_for_fast_kernel threshold (or ship a lightweight fast kernel for size 1-2).

claire: I'm going to toggle prefer-latency=false on the canary pool (10%) and watch. Applying now.

deploy-bot: rollout: canary change applied to pool 'canary-runtime-10pct' at 07:40 by claire

claire: Early signal: p50 on canary is back to baseline within 3 minutes after toggle. KV hit-rate on canary recovered too. Keeping canary for 30m then will expand if stable.

matt: Good. If that stays, we should make the heuristic conservative for small-seq traffic by default and add a telemetry alarm for microbatch-size distribution (alert when size1 fraction > 20%).

anuj: Agreed. I'll also capture a focused trace showing kernel routing decision for size=1 to see how often we route to the slower kernel vs a fast path. Might help us decide whether to change kernel thresholds vs batching.

henry: I'll open an RFC to: 
- bump token_budget_target floor for small-seq contexts
- add a metric and alert for microbatch starvation
- evaluate a tiny-batch kernel (size 1-2) or relax current routing rule
Assigning to eng-runtime owners.

matt: Thanks all. Follow-ups:
- anuj: get focused kernel-routing traces + KV miss correlation
- claire: monitor canary for 30m and post metrics
- henry: RFC and proposed thresholds

claire: early thumbs up on canary :thumbsup:

matt: nice work, keeping an eye. :chart_with_downwards_trend:

perf-bot: note: incident-ticket #INC-2026-451 auto-created for investigation (owner: eng-runtime)

anuj: sample KV log lines (for thread): `CACHE_MISS session=abcd1234 ctx_len=512` `CACHE_EVICT session=abcd1234 victim=0x7f8a`

henry: FYI we should also consider adding a small hysteresis to the budget floor so rapid toggles in traffic don't flip aggressively.

matt: Agreed. Will sync in weekly runtime sync, and we can fast-track RFC if canary holds.

claire: will post a short summary to #eng-runtime when rollout decision is final.
